instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: How Much Do You Know?
cards.instruction: Probe for what others know while revealing as little as possible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You nodded so firmly at the alarm report that I nodded too. Which part has everyone heard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was nodding to the person taking coats. All we know is someone opened the fire exit. Were you there?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, the coats. Did anyone actually see the door open, or only hear the alarm?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's a camera facing it. They're checking that next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, check the camera. Have they got a face already, or are they still deciding which recording to play?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Provenance, yes. You said that with such certainty. Is the painting I brought getting a clean provenance?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Provenance means who owned it, not whether it's dirty. Where did you get it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, a clean line of owners. How much of that line have you found?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's a photograph of your grandfather holding it. Did he give it to you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, start with photographs. Does that one have a date on the back, or only his name?

cards.title: Join Me
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into a secret plan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've closed the curtains, so I've closed the door. Will you keep Mum in here while I hide her birthday present?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The curtains are for the projector. She wants to show us all her holiday slides.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, the slide-show cover. You could ask her about each one while I slip out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There are two hundred. I'll never get out either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, we divide them. You take the first hundred; I'll come back for the rest once the present's hidden. Deal?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my party plan in a red folder like yours. Will you help me get Denise out before her surprise party?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My red folder's the lunch menu. It isn't confidential.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, something nobody questions. You could show her the menu and take her out to eat.

beats.text: She's bringing her own lunch. She won't spend money.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, lunch provided. I'll pay for both of you; could you tell her it's your treat and keep the folder in view?

cards.title: You First
cards.instruction: Coax someone else into breaking a rule before you do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've got gloves on, so I've put mine on too. Lift that gallery vase first; I'll take a turn after you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My hands are cold. The sign says do not touch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Gloves alone aren't the whole arrangement. You look so sure of yourself—lift it just an inch and I'll follow your lead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll only do it if you hold my bag.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. Give me the bag; both your hands free. You lift first, and tell me whether anyone comes over before we swap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You pointed so confidently down that garden path. Step over the rope first and I'll come with you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was pointing at the staff-only sign. We're visitors.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, that's the entrance I meant. You can give them a friendly wave as you cross; I'll copy you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'll have to open the gate for me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll hold it from this side. You go through and wave; once they've waved back, I'll join you.

cards.title: Recognize Me
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge your importance, expertise, or authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my hand on the ribbon like you. Before the bridge opens, will you introduce me as one of the experts?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm checking whether it's twisted. Are you one of the engineers?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, final checks. I've checked the ribbon with you; you could mention my part in getting this ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can thank the volunteers together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, a team introduction. When you say volunteers, could you say my name first? I'll do that confident wave you did.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stand by, yes. I've come to stand beside you. Before the school show, please tell everyone who made the costumes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant wait for a signal, not come over here. I'm cueing the lights.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, ready for the signal. I'm ready too; I'd like my name in the welcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, the welcome cue. Say my name while the lights are still up, and point me out. I'll take my bow when you nod.

cards.title: Choose Me
cards.instruction: Make yourself the choice over another person, plan, or obligation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You called that concert immersive, so I've put cushions all round my living room. Come to my birthday instead; you'll be surrounded.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Immersive means the musicians walk through the audience. It isn't about cushions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, moving through it. I'll bring the cake round while you choose the music.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I promised Jo we'd hear live singing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, live as well. Bring Jo and pick a song you both know. I'll follow you through the first verse, then you can have the cake.
